scope: 54 reference entries in this expansion, including partial-access and unresolved/candidate entries. Earlier targeted corrections retained in phase-reconciliation-current-20261002.md. Not a completed every-entry/full-text bibliography review or validation of LIMEN phase mappings. Experimental framework retained per D-028/D-029.

rows.method: Experienced meditators and matched controls, several meditation tasks
rows.finding: Primary identity verified; retrieved record excerpt did not include complete results. Publisher direct access failed. Ayahuasca paper discussion describes meditation as stronger anterior/posterior coupling.

rows.method: Meditators/controls, meditation versus active cognitive task
rows.finding: Reduced DMN activation beyond active task, group-by-task effects in posterior cingulate/precuneus and ACC.
rows.disposition: Retain task-specific activation finding; does not measure durable phase restructuring.

rows.method: Human psilocybin ASL/BOLD fMRI; publisher full text inspected
rows.finding: Reduced hub blood flow/BOLD and mPFC-PCC coupling under acute psilocybin.
rows.disposition: Retain acute imaging result; vascular signal is not a direct neurotransmitter measurement or permanent topology change.

rows.method: Twenty healthy participants, LSD/placebo ASL/BOLD/MEG; usable fMRI15 and MEG14; publisher full text inspected
rows.finding: Reduced within-network integrity and changed between-network communication; DMN integrity and PH-RSC coupling related to ego dissolution.
rows.disposition: Preserve distinct activity, integrity, segregation and subjective measures; not global destruction or terminal unit loss.

rows.finding: Proposes increased entropy/criticality and altered DMN organization in primary states.

rows.method: Before/after treatment,19 patients with usable paired imaging16, psychological support
rows.finding: Post-treatment within-DMN connectivity increased; selected connections associated with five-week clinical response.
rows.disposition: Retain contextual recovery observation and proposed reset mechanism; not demonstrated novel DMN topology or generic P10 renewal. Source bibliography omits last author Nutt.

rows.method: Ten experienced ayahuasca users, final imaging9, before/after; primary full text inspected
rows.finding: Reduced core DMN activity and PCC/precuneus connectivity; mPFC-PCC change and DMN-TPN relationship not significant.
rows.disposition: Retain localized measured result; avoid uniform claim that all DMN connections decrease.

rows.method: Perfusion fMRI in27 people, adaptive arithmetic versus boredom/overload
rows.finding: Flow associated with increased IFG/putamen activity and decreased mPFC/amygdala activity.

rows.finding: Proposes transient hypofrontality and implicit/explicit processing distinction.
rows.disposition: Retain hypothesis; not independent neuroimaging confirmation.

rows.finding: Frontal/parietal/left caudate activity changes during glossolalia; abstract does not specify direction for each region.

rows.finding: Challenge/recovery cycles, ketosis and signaling pathways associated with plasticity and resilience; publisher correction listed in2020.

rows.method: Open-label single one-hour float session,50 anxiety/stress participants, self-report
rows.finding: Reported anxiety and negative affect declined after session.

rows.method: Group-drumming intervention/control study,111 volunteers across preliminary/final cohorts
rows.finding: DHEA/cortisol ratio and selected immune-cell activity increased; anxiety/depression scales unchanged.

rows.method: Covert single-word repetition fMRI in23 nonmeditators

rows.method: Opioid-ligand PET in10 athletes, rest versus after two-hour running
rows.finding: Reduced opioid-receptor availability correlated with euphoria in frontolimbic regions.

rows.method: Cold-exposure autonomic study; metadata and publisher introduction retrieved

rows.method: Review including women with complete spinal-cord injury and fMRI during cervical stimulation/orgasm

rows.method: Merged male/female PET datasets during genital stimulation/orgasm
